about.title: Pacifica Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Coastal towns like Pacifica come with fog, salt air, and drainage issues that can turn ordinary walkways into hazards — a puddled entryway, a broken step outside a Sharp Park Road business, or uneven flooring in a store off SR-1. When a property owner ignores these conditions and someone gets hurt, California law allows the injured person to seek compensation, but only if they can show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't act. That's often the hardest part of these cases, and it's why documentation matters so much early on. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects people injured on someone else's property with an independent local attorney who can look at the specifics of what happened, gather the right evidence, and explain the options. There's no cost to get matched, and no obligation to move forward. If your fall happened in Pacifica, a quick conversation can help you understand where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in a Pacifica Fall Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew (or Should Have Known)
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or repeat conditions that support this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Pacifica businesses along Rt 1 and Cabrillo Highway overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can be the difference between a strong claim and no evidence at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly rather than let blame get exaggerated.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Pacifica?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity owns the property — like a city sidewalk or public building — the deadline is much shorter, often just six months. It's worth having someone review your specific situation early so you don't lose the option to pursue a claim.

items.question: What if I fell at a store or restaurant near Sharp Park Road and no one saw it happen?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't automatically end a claim. Photos of the hazard, incident reports, receipts showing you were there, and surveillance footage from the business can all help reconstruct what happened. An independent attorney can help figure out what evidence still exists and how to request it before it's lost.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service — we're not a law firm, and we don't charge you to get matched with an independent attorney in our network. Attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
